newsitem.title: ESTONIA: TARTU BREWERY TO ISSUE SHARES, GET LISTING.
newsitem.headline: TARTU BREWERY TO ISSUE SHARES, GET LISTING.

text.p: Estonian beer maker Tartu Brewery, in which Finnish Olvi has a 15 percent stake, said on Wednesday it would this year make a share issue and was planning to obtain a stock market listing.
"Starting this year we are going to make another share issue and will be going to the Tallin stock exchange," Tartu Brewery board member Aho Anttila told Reuters in an interview.
"We are now working with a corporate finance company in Tallin but no final agreement has been signed as yet," he added.
He said that some 25 percent of the share capital would be issued, the minimum to get a listing on the stock market.
Some 85 percent of the company's shares are owned by the Magnum Group, a conglomerate that is involved in various business sectors.
"The details are to be decided at our shareholder meeting, wjhich will happen in mid-May. The minimum will be 25 percent of the share capital," he added.
Olvi bought its stake in Tartu in October last year.
Tartu, based in the southern town of Tartu, has set its sight on capturing more of the Estonian market, dominated by Saku, part of the Baltic Beverage group.
Baltic Beverage is itself a joint venture of Hartwall and Pripps, owned by Norway's Orkla and Volvo .
Tartu has share capital of 7.5 million kroons and in 1995 its turnover was 175 million kroons. More recent figures were not immediately available.
